subject: Standby GPU pool: temporary reservation + autoscale exception request
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Standby pool request: QuantumHealth pilot (July 20–Aug 3)

Team —

Quick ask: QuantumHealth has locked a live demo week starting Jul 20 that requires consistently low inference latency. They want a short pilot run (2 weeks + a 3–day shadow before) that must not be interrupted by preemption during business hours.

Request details (high level):
- Duration: Jul 20 00:00 -> Aug 3 23:59 (UTC window — US west primary)
- Desired steady capacity: 4 GPU slots (A100-equivalent); expected burst to 6 for 30m windows during demo days
- Autoscale exception: avoid reclaim/preemption for the reserved window between 08:00–18:00 PT on demo days
- Why: customer-facing live demo, strict SLA for P99 latency, we cannot rely on fallback to a quantized model during the demo

Attached: standby_request_template.xlsx (filled), capacity-snapshot-20260713.csv, draft demo-runbook.md

Asks:
1) Can allocations/ops provision a temporary standby reservation or carveout for this window?
2) What is the approval path and expected lead time? Do we need a formal PO / procurement sign-off before you can reserve?
3) Cost ballpark for guaranteed + burst (so we can commit back to the customer)

If this can be done with a mixed model (2 guaranteed + 2 burst on top) that would be OK; I flagged the full 4 to be conservative. Happy to hop on a 20m call.

—
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby pool request: QuantumHealth pilot (July 20–Aug 3)

David —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before I greenlight escalation to allocations/ops:
- Expected steady token QPS and concurrency per slot during the peak 30m windows? (need to size buffer and KV cache impact)
- Is there a viable fallback model we can run if we do get partial preemption (e.g., smaller model that still meets demo objectives)?
- Is this demo under an active deal where we can charge for dedicated standby? If so, pass the deal id.

Operationally, we typically prefer a split approach: 2 guaranteed reservations + a burst lane for the remaining capacity. Autoscale exceptions are costly (both ops burden and unit economics) so engineering/product should confirm willingness to absorb incremental cost.

Marcus/Hannah — can you confirm lead times if we file a Bridge request? If ops needs a PO, David please loop procurement.

Kimberly
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 12:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby pool request: QuantumHealth pilot (Jul20–Aug3) — allocation notes

Quick notes from allocation side:
- We can stage a "standby carve" using two guaranteed slots + two burst-capable slots for the requested window. Burst slots will live in the preemptible pool but tagged with a short-term lease — this reduces total cost while giving best-effort headroom.
- Autoscale exception to prevent preemption across the full business-day window is operationally heavier: Ops will need a maintenance blackout and explicit SLA carve (this requires Bridge approval and a 48–72h lead).
- Cost estimate (rough): guaranteed slot ~ $1,200/day each; burst slot (best-effort) ~ $400/day each when used. For a 15-day window: guaranteed 2 * $1,200 * 15 = $36,000; burst buffer (2 slots used for 30m/day on demo days) estimator ~ $2,400 — net depends on actual burst usage.

Action items I need:
- Final confirmation on steady QPS/concurrency + list of fallback models you can run
- Confirm if QuantumHealth will sign an addendum (deal id provided) or if Product absorbs cost

If you want a guaranteed no-preempt window for all 4 slots, escalate now and I'll file JIRA-OPS-1234 (Bridge). Otherwise I can provision the mixed-mode carve with shorter lead (24h).

—Marcus
Capacity Allocations Lead

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby pool request: QuantumHealth pilot (Jul20–Aug3)

On Wed, Jul 14, 2026 at 09:12, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick ask: QuantumHealth has locked a live demo week starting Jul 20 that requires consistently low inference latency. They want a short pilot run (2 weeks + a 3–day shadow before) that must not be interrupted by preemption during business hours.

Thanks — to confirm: the live demo is customer-facing and the purchase decision could be made within two weeks after the demo. We need reliability for the demo itself; partial preemption would risk the sale.

Requirements from Product:
- We need a no-preempt window for core demo hours (09:00–17:00 PT) on Jul 21, 22 and Jul 27, 28 (these are the days the customer will stress)
- Backup plan: run a quantized fallback if absolutely necessary, but it must be a last resort; training team has already validated one smaller model that maintains 95% of quality for non-audio traffic
- Runbook: I'll send a short runbook with exact endpoints, health-checks, and a roll-back plan by EOD.

We are OK absorbing cost for 2 guaranteed slots; for the remaining 2 we should prefer burst unless Marcus confirms a cheap carver. David — please start procurement loop if we need PO.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Core Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby GPU pool: temporary reservation + autoscale exception request — agreed plan

Summary / agreed plan after the thread:
- Provision strategy: 2 guaranteed slots (A100 eq) + 2 burst-tagged slots (best-effort) for Jul 20 -> Aug 3.
- Autoscale exception: will request a limited no-preempt window for 09:00–17:00 PT on the four high-risk demo days (Jul 21, 22, 27, 28) via Bridge (JIRA-OPS-1234). That keeps ops burden limited and gives Product the reliability they need.
- Financials: Product to cover guaranteed slot cost for the window; Kimberly to confirm internal chargeback. Marcus to send final cost estimate to David by EOD tomorrow.
- Next steps:
  * Marcus: file JIRA-OPS-1234 (Bridge request) and include capacity-snapshot-20260713.csv
  * David: open procurement ticket / PO request referencing deal QH-PLT-2026-004 and DocuSign-Request-789
  * Laura: send final runbook + list of fallback models (demo-runbook-draft.md)
  * Hannah: schedule a maintenance blackout for the no-preempt windows and confirm on-call coverage

If no objections, I'll proceed with procurement and CC the customer.

Thanks everyone —
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
